order: Frozen by its own commit before learner, benchmark/test implementations or access to scores. Do not tune thresholds after inspecting results without precommitting a new protocol and cohort.
question: Does an engineered error-count horizon policy retain fast early B adaptation while recovering the later B stability of recent32 and B->A archived skill, despite unannounced same-schema reversals?
simulator: Exactly same authored two-key SameSchemaWorld from the prior study: original A (240 independent training episodes), reversed B (64), original A again (48), with unchanged inlet/outlet features/action frame across stages and no hidden phase data given to learner.
source: Oldest 192 public outcome observations define immutable archive, learned by RelationOutcomeMemory using engineered value span max-min; no true change points, scenario IDs or labels stored by learner.

algorithm.surprise: An event is surprising when anchor's smoothed likelihood of the observed public progress/damage/neutral class is below 0.125.
algorithm.newest_four: Count surprises among last four outcomes; count all last eight and last32.
algorithm.gate: If latest four surprises >=2 or latest four surprises==1 and last eight surprises>=3, do not use anchor; otherwise use archive anchor.
algorithm.adaptive_horizon: When gate is open, choose newest 32 outcomes if last 32 contain >=15 surprises relative to anchor, otherwise newest 8 outcomes. No hardcoded elapsed phase times or access to hidden regime. Model fits on all chosen events, including triggering evidence; these are NOT independent model-selection data.
algorithm.abstain: Never abstain in this experimental candidate; an always-abstain policy remains explicit and counted as failed tasks.
algorithm.replay: Append-only public three-field evidence, exact same feature-key set, bound MAX_SAMPLES, SHA256 checkpoint and replay; no default promotion or autonomous training actions.

success_criteria: At B8, seek at least 165/180 successes (fast_shock baseline) and at B32,B48,B64 seek >=170/180, better than fast_shock on average; return-A4 seek >=170/180 and archive retention. Disclose if recent32, recent8, or legacy is better at any checkpoint and report all harms, abstentions, acquisition costs. No promotion regardless of score.
provenance: One seed-isolated external random actor first-action observation per disposable TRAIN episode; count harmful actor interventions exactly once, separate from harmful read-only TEST simulated actions. All policies see matched training history, holdout episodes never train.
limitations: Fixed short/long windows and surprise cutoffs are developer choices, not autonomously discovered appropriate timescales.
Same simplistic manually authored deterministic symmetric A-B-A range-rule reversal; not unknown independent domains or stochastic real-world processes.
Recent models train on the same observations used to choose them, risking selection overfit.
No safe first contact possible without B outcome observations; measure harm explicitly.
No real-world authority, promotion, GitHub PR merge, source authentication, AthenZ/Synveil integration, or D1-D10/V2A/V2B roadmap changes.
